newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI strike in Bombay continues as talks fail.
newsitem.headline: India SBI strike in Bombay continues as talks fail.

text.p: Talks between agitating officers of the State Bank of India (SBI) and the management failed on Tuesday, a spokesman of the officers' association told Reuters.
"We had discussions with the management," he said. "There was no progress. Our action plan stays."
The strike at SBI's offices in Bombay entered its fifth day on Tuesday.
The SBI Officers' Federation has called for a strike at 13 regional headquarters on June 19, the spokesman said.
The strike, which began at the Bombay head office, has now spread to the western states of Maharashtra (of which Bombay is the capital) and Goa.

The strike began on June 12 at the Bombay office to protest against the suspension of three officers accused of failure to follow procedures in handling accounts of CRB Capital Markets, a finance company now facing liquidation proceedings.
SBI's board is meeting in Calcutta on June 19 to finalise accounts for the year ended March 31, 1997.
The bank official said the strike would be extended to SBI's countrywide branches on June 23 if the dispute continues.
